The nanoparticles, were assumed embedded in a Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> layer. Using Maxwell Garnett model and WKB approximation, the direct tunneling current and the I-V characteristics were simulated. The simulated Flatband voltage shift was compared with recent experimental results.

articleTitle: Effects of post annealing temperatures on the properties of Sr0.6Ba0.4Nb2O6 thin films
abstract: Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</inf>Ba<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> (SBN) thin films were deposited using radio frequency (RF) magnetron sputtering method and post annealing in a conventional furnace. The annealing process had improved the crystallization and also had large influences on the crystalline orientation. As the annealing temperature increased from 600<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>C to 700<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>C, the diffraction intensities of (410) and (001) planes increased. Annealed at 800<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>C, the SBN thin films showed highly c-axis crystalline orientation of (001) plane. The influences of annealing temperatures on the electrical characteristics of the polarization-applied electric field curves, the capacitance-voltage curves, and the leakage current density-electric field curves were investigated.

articleTitle: The analysis of AZO films made by a magnetic controlled DC sputtering system
abstract: Magnetic controlled dc sputtering method was used in the deposition of Al-doped ZnO (AZO) transparent conducting thin films. Effects of different process parameters, such as working pressure and substrate temperature, and compare properties of AZO films with RF sputtering in order to obtain best process parameters. Over 80% the transmittance of AZO film are observed at visible region (380 ~ 780 nm) with DC sputtering. The refraction decreased with increasing substrate temperature while the grain size, carrier concentration and carrier mobility increased with increasing substrate temperature.

articleTitle: Photoresponse of Zinc oxide thin-film transistors with location-controlled crystal grains fabricated by low-temperature hydrothermal method
abstract: Zinc oxide (ZnO) bottom-gate (BG) thin-film transistors (TFTs) with single vertical grain boundary in the channel have been successfully fabricated by a novel low-temperature (i.e. 85 °C) hydrothermal method. The proposed devices demonstrated the high field-effect mobility of 9.07 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/V·s, low threshold voltage of 2.25 V, high on/off current ratio above 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>, and superior current drivability, attributed to the high-quality ZnO channel with single grain boundary. Moreover, a stable and repeatable operation of dynamic photoresponse is observed for the location-controlled hydrothermally grown ZnO BG-TFTs.

articleTitle: Chloride ion selective electrode for detection of low chloride ion concentration
abstract: In this study, the ruthenium dioxide (RuO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) thin film was deposited on silicon (Si) substrate by radio frequency (R. F.) sputtering system. In order to optimize the sensing property of the chloride ion sensing device, the chloride ion selective membrane was prepared on sensing window of Si/RuO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensing device by dropping and spin coating methods, respectively. Furthermore, the chloride ion selective membrane was prepared by spin coating with different spinning rates, and the sensing property of chloride ion sensing device relating with spinning rate was investigated.

articleTitle: Preparation of biomimetic nanofibers by electrospinning of blends of silk fibroin and chitosan for bone tissue engineering
abstract: In this study, we have successfully fabricated electrospun bead-free silk fibroin (SF)/chitosan (CS) blend nanofibers (NFs) covering the whole range of CS content (0, 25, 50, 75, and 100%). NFs are treated with ethanol/ammonia aqueous solution to remove residual TFA and to change SF protein conformation. After the chemical treatment, SF/CS NFs could maintain the original structure for up to 54 days in culture medium. Human fetal osteoblast progenitor (hFOB) cells were capable of proliferating and osteogenic differentiating on SF/CS NFs from MTS and alkaline phosphatase assays. SF enhanced hFOB proliferation while CS enhanced hFOB differentiation. The prepared SF/CS blend NFs will be suitable for tissue engineering applications.

articleTitle: Developing the properties of polyvinylidene fluoride/(Ba0.8Sr0.2)(Ti0.9Zr0.1)O3 composite films for embedded capacitors using
abstract: The average particle sizes of nanoscale (Ba<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</inf>Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>)(Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</inf> Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>)O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> ceramic powder (nano-BSTZ) was approximately 73nm. Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)/nano-BSTZ composite films with various contents of the nano-BSTZ were screen-printed on indium tin oxide glass substrates. From the XRD patterns, PVDF was the semicrystalline type polymer. The content of the nano-BSTZ increased from 10 wt% to 50 wt%, the dielectric constants of the PVDF/nano-BSTZ films slightly decreased with increasing measured frequency. The specific capacitance values of the PVDF/nano-BSTZ composite films mixing with 50 wt% nano-BSTZ was 11.6 nF/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (measured at 1 kHz). Those results suggested that the PVDF/nano-BSTZ composite films were a good candidate to develop thinner embedded capacitor devices with higher capacitance value.

articleTitle: Growth of few wall carbon nanotubes with narrow diameter distribution over Fe-Mo-MgO catalyst by methane/acetylene catalytic decomposition
abstract: We report of few wall carbon nanotubes (FWNT) growth by methane/acetylene decomposition over bimetallic Fe-Mo catalyst with MgO support. Our transmission electron microscopy investigation (TEM) shows high purity and narrow diameter distribution of grown nanotubes. The phase analysis of CNT product was performed by X-ray and Mossbauer techniques.

articleTitle: Study of temperature effects of mobility, swing, and early voltages on strained MOSFET devices
abstract: In addition to global stained epitaxial SiGe layer, silicon nitride as contact etching stop layer (CESL) is to be deposited on the whole device to enhance the straining effects. As found in this paper, 10μm/10μm (channel length/ width) PMOS devices at various temperatures with or without stain are referred. To focus on the SiGe alone, the 1.5nm silicon cap following epi-taxial SiGe is to be considered leaving the channel mainly SiGe. The mobility and swing are determined and compared with the control wafers without strained engineering. The variations of Early voltages at different temperatures are taken into account, too. Regularity of Early Voltage variations shows the potential implicit physical meanings as the strained engineering is to be applied.

articleTitle: Study on NH3 plasma-treated polyimide/MWNT composites on electrical and surface properties
abstract: In this work, we study the surface modification of polyimide/MWNT composites by plasma treatment. After the NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> plasma treatment, the surface properties of polyimide containing MWNT (U-CNT) or acid modified MWNT (M-CNT) were investigated by XPS, XRD, contact angle and electrical measurements. The surface of polyimide/MWNT composites was examined to be more hydrophilic after the NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> plasma treatment, which can therefore improve the surface electrical conductivity of the polyimide/MWNT composites. The XRD results further indicated that the formation of MWNT network structure in polyimide matrix impeded the motion of polyimide molecules.

articleTitle: Investigation of post-annealing treatment on barrier layers for passivation flexible organic light-emitting diode
abstract: Fluorinated silicon dioxide films by liquid phase deposition method were coated on plastic substrate as a moisture barrier layer. By the measurement of Fourier transform infrared absorption spectroscopy, the water-absorbed related peak was found after severe water-vapor test. After annealing under N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> ambiences, the water-absorbed related peaks disappear and ability of resisting water absorption can be enhanced.

articleTitle: The complex nanostructure of P(VDF-TrFE) made by dual step hot-embossing
abstract: In this work, complex 3D ferroelectric nanostructures on Poly(vinylidenefluoride-trifluoroethylene), P(VDF-TrFE), films have successfully been fabricated using a special hot-embossing process with two sequential shots on the same site with a grating template and a dot array template of the same periodicity at the same hot-embossing temperature. The nanostructures have been characterized with atomic force microscope (AFM), piezoresponse force microscope (PFM) and Fourier transformed infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). It is shown that sequential hot-embossing offers an effective way to fabricate complex 3D nanostructures of functional ferroelectric materials toward various applications.

articleTitle: Potentiometric nano-grained TiO2: Ru-based nafion/uric acid biosensor
abstract: The potentiometric nafion/uric acid biosensor formed on nano-grained ruthenium-doped titanium dioxide (TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>: Ru) sensing film are proposed in this investigation, which is employed to detect the uric acid concentration in the phosphate buffered saline (PBS) solution. SEM and XRD are used for observing surface morphology and crystalline phase of TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>: Ru sensing film. The uricase (EC 1.7.3.3, 14.5 unit/mg) immobilized on 2 mm × 2 mm sensing area of the TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>: Ru-based electrode by using the mixture of 3-glycidyloxypropyltrimethoxysilane (GPTS) and toluene with the volume ratio (GPTS : toluene = 1 : 4) is presented. The nafion/UA biosensor is measured in PBS uric acid solutions ranging between 2 mg/dl and 10 mg/dl whose sensitivity and linearity are 4.02 mV/(mg/dl) and 0.999, respectively.

articleTitle: Local field enhancement dependence on nanoparticle's geometry in Au/TiO2/Ti/Si SERS-active substrate for biochemical sensors
abstract: In this work, we study the effect of surface roughness and shape of Au nanoparticles on the local field enhancement of SERS-active substrates. Our 3D FDTD simulation predicts that the substrate with roughened surface exhibits large field enhancement, especially for cubic shape of nanoparticle. The field enhancement of spherical and cubic nanoparticles is enlarged by Au/Ag alloy and Au nanocage structure which is useful for biochemical sensing applications.

articleTitle: A unique art purifying the atomic scale, zone selective, and quantitative information of bonding and electronic dynamics at sites surrounding defects, surfaces, and interfaces
abstract: With the theory enabled technology, we have been able to purify information from zones up to two atomic spacings regarding the evolution of the bond length, bond strength, energy density, and the energetic behavior of the localized core and valence electrons by filtering out the bulk and background information, which enabled us to identify the direction of charge flow in the catalytic reactions between the gaseous specimens and the Rh and Pt adatoms catalysts, and between the gaseous specimens and the CuPd and AgPd nanoalloys. With the special technique, we have also been able to clarify that the Dirac-Fermi polarons detected using STM/S as high protrusions with resonance at Fermi energy as arising from the polarization of the unpaired dangling-bond electrons by the undercoordination-induced local densification and quantum entrapment of the energetically low-lying electrons, which in turn screen and split the crystal potential adding another extra component in the upper edge of the core band.

articleTitle: Source/drain doping influence on heterojunction graphene nanoribbon tunneling field effect transistors
abstract: We investigate the device performance of heterojunction graphene nanoribbons tunneling field-effect transistors as a function of the doping concentrations based on the non-equilibrium Green's function. We observe that variation in source doping changes the OFF-non-equilibrium Green's functionstate currents (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</sub>), the ON-state currents (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</sub>) and the subthreshold slope (SS) significantly while variation in drain doping changes mainly the I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</sub>. Additionally, low SS and large I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</sub>/I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</sub> ratio can be achieved by applying proper asymmetric source-drain doping.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic characteristics of MOS structure with photo enhanced trap assist tunneling current by oxide etching
abstract: In this work, MOS photovoltaic mechanism with side wall trap-assist tunneling path by oxide etching was demonstrated. It was clearly observed that the photo response of device with oxide etching is tremendously enhanced with respect to that without. The efficiency of MOS photovoltaic with side wall trap-assist tunneling is strongly dependent on the etched potion of oxide. The perimeter of electrode is critical for MOS photovoltaic application.

articleTitle: Micro electrode array with needle structure for brain focal cooling
abstract: Cooling is a potential treatment for epilepsy diseases without any electric current pass through the organization of brain. The module is integrated with micro-electrodes and thermo-electric cooler. It was fabricated and utilized inside a rat brain. It can make cooling location deeper in order to improve the diagnosis of focal epilepsy. We are currently determining the efficacy of local cooling for the therapy of certain focal epilepsies.

articleTitle: Nasopharyngeal cancer cell death induced by high-dose gold nanoparticles
abstract: This study investigated if gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) could be used as a new therapeutic agent for NPC by evaluating their anti-tumor effect in vitro. AuNPs prepared in this study had an average diameter of 20.5 nm and they were observed under light microscopy as dark material aggregated in the cells after treatment. The AuNPs reduced cell viability in a concentration-dependant manner by Trypan Blue assay: 74.7% at 50 μM, 39.0% at 100μM, and 7.1% at 200 μM, respectively. TUNEL stain was positive in AuNP-treated cells. The AuNP possess specific imaging properties and is cytotoxic to NPC cells at high concentrations.
